newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fortis Q1 net seen up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fortis Q1 net seen up 18 pct.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis is expected to announce on Wednesday a rise of almost 18 percent in net profit for the first quarter of 1997 to some 185 million ECU, analysts said.
Fortis' net profit a year ago was 157 million ECU.
Analysts said the recently acquired Dutch merchant bank MeesPierson was expected to boost profits and they also saw continued growth in life insurance and a further upturn in non-life results.
"I see the acquisition of MeesPierson as an overwhelming plus sign," said Tom Muller of NIBStrating.
Fortis bought MeesPierson from ABN AMRO for 2.5 billion guilders.
Muller said it was not only the acquisition of MeesPierson that lifted Fortis results strongly. "Car insurance in the Netherlands and Belgium should be substantially better," he said.
He added that accident and health activities in the United States were expected to recover further.

Daan Worm of ING Barings said he expected the group's accident and health pre-tax profits to rise to some 10 million ECU in the first quarter of 1997 versus 2 million ECU in the same period a year earlier as health activities in the United States had been loss making in the first three months of 1996.
Analysts said the group's life business units should continue their growth path.
Fortis' 50 percent shareholder, Fortis Amev, is expected to announce an increase in first quarter net profits of 16.2 percent to nearly 199 million guilders, analysts said.
They said it was difficult to give a precise forecast for Fortis results as the result from realised and unrealised capital gains and losses differed from quarter to quarter.
In the first quarter of 1996 the group's operating result from realised and unrealised capital gains was 34 million ECU versus 12 million ECU in the first quarter of 1995.
Analysts said they expected realised and unrealised capital gains in 1997, minus exceptional revenues and charges, to be some 60 million ECU, about equal to the 1996 outcome.
Muller of NIBStrating was very upbeat on the group's 1997 results as he foresaw a rise in full-year profits of about 22 percent.
"Organic growth should be above 12-13 percent and on top of this comes MeesPierson," he said.
